rows.applies_to: buyer's agents, first home, property search, broker value
rows.hook: For a first home, a buyer's agent is rarely worth the fee.
rows.so_what: Ask what you'd get for that one to two percent that you couldn't do yourself with good data.
rows.insight: For a first home bought in the general market, we don't think a buyer's agent is worth the roughly $15k–$20k fee. Instead we support buyers with property data, due diligence and negotiation while they do the inspecting themselves.
rows.why: Buyer's agents charge around one to two percent of the price and make more sense on high-ticket purchases of a million-plus; for a home to live in, how you feel when you inspect a place matters most.
rows.source: Plaud: 09-07 Consultation: Mercedes - First Home Purchase (2026-09-07); Plaud: 08-06 Customer Consultation: Nurse Prospect Misunderstanding of Mortgage Brokerage vs Buyer's Agent (2026-08-06)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: first home, broker value, negotiation, due diligence
rows.hook: Buying your first home? The loan is the easy bit.
rows.so_what: Ask your broker what they do between pre-approval and keys, not just what rate they get.
rows.insight: For first-home buyers, our job isn't just the loan. We help interpret property data, check whether a place is good value, help with offers and negotiation, and make sure the contract terms are right, all the way to getting the keys.
rows.why: Buying a first home is a big financial decision, and the hardest part is usually finding and assessing the property rather than getting the finance.
rows.source: Plaud: 10-09 Call with Quan: First-Time Homebuyer Loan Strategy (2026-10-09); Plaud: 08-06 Customer Consultation: Nurse Prospect Misunderstanding of Mortgage Brokerage vs Buyer's Agent (2026-08-06); Plaud: 09-07 Consultation: First-Home Purchase Strategy and Borrowing Capacity for Pilot and Event Manager (2026-09-07)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: first home guarantee, low deposit, savings buffer, LMI
rows.hook: Qualify for a 5% deposit scheme? Use it and keep your savings.
rows.so_what: Ask whether a smaller deposit and a bigger buffer leaves you better off than tipping everything in.
rows.insight: If you qualify for a low-deposit (5%) first home scheme, we often prefer using it and keeping part of your savings as a backup, rather than putting everything into the deposit.
rows.why: A lower deposit means you have to borrow more, so you need enough borrowing capacity. But holding back savings gives a buffer that people value, and it can sit in an offset.
rows.source: Plaud: 09-07 Consultation: Mercedes - First Home Purchase (2026-09-07); Plaud: 10-09 Call with Quan: First-Time Homebuyer Loan Strategy (2026-10-09)

rows.applies_to: employment, contracting, self-employed income, borrowing capacity, timing
rows.hook: Changing jobs before you buy? Take the permanent role.
rows.so_what: If a purchase is close, ask how a job change would be treated before you accept it.
rows.insight: If you're planning to buy soon and you're changing jobs anyway, a permanent salaried role gets you there faster than contracting. Lenders treat contract income as self-employed income, which needs a track record before it counts.
rows.why: Permanent salary can be used almost immediately, while contracting income needs history and tax returns, which can push your purchase back by a year.
rows.source: Plaud: 09-07 Consultation: Mercedes - First Home Purchase (2026-09-07)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: self-employed, tax returns, borrowing capacity
rows.hook: Minimising your tax now can cost you a house later.
rows.so_what: If you're self-employed and buying within two years, ask your accountant how the next return will read to a bank.
rows.insight: If you're self-employed or contracting and plan to buy in the next year or two, don't shy away from reporting your income. Build your tax returns so the income can actually be used when you apply.
rows.why: Lenders assess what's on your tax returns, so minimising reported income now reduces what you can borrow later.
rows.source: Plaud: 09-07 Consultation: Mercedes - First Home Purchase (2026-09-07)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: borrowing capacity, rule of thumb, HECS
rows.hook: Roughly five times your income is where borrowing power starts.
rows.so_what: Use it to set a search budget, then get the real number run through several lenders.
rows.insight: As a rough rule of thumb, borrowing capacity is about five times your income, before adjusting for things like HECS and other debts.
rows.why: It gives buyers a quick budget to start searching with before we run the full numbers.
rows.source: Plaud: 09-07 Consultation: Mercedes - First Home Purchase (2026-09-07)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: car loans, personal debt, borrowing capacity, savings
rows.hook: Got savings and a car loan? Clear the car first.
rows.so_what: Ask what paying out the car loan, break fee included, does to your borrowing power.
rows.insight: If you have healthy savings and a car loan, paying the car loan off before applying is often a no-brainer, even if there's a payout or break fee.
rows.why: Car loan repayments eat into borrowing capacity and the interest is usually higher than any break cost, so clearing it leaves only the mortgage to worry about.
rows.source: Plaud: 10-09 Call with Quan: First-Time Homebuyer Loan Strategy (2026-10-09)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: first home owner grant, new apartments, off-the-plan
rows.hook: Don't buy a brand-new apartment just to get the grant.
rows.so_what: Compare the grant against what you'd overpay for new before it decides your purchase.
rows.insight: We wouldn't chase the first home owner grant by buying a brand-new apartment just to qualify for it.
rows.why: New apartments tend to be overpriced and inflated, so the grant can be outweighed by what you overpay.
rows.source: Plaud: 09-07 Consultation: Mercedes - First Home Purchase (2026-09-07)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: apartments, body corporate, due diligence, units
rows.hook: There's always a reason someone's selling. Find it before you buy.
rows.so_what: Read the body corporate minutes and ask what the last three special levies were for.
rows.insight: With apartments, especially in sought-after inner suburbs, we do very detailed due diligence on the body corporate, because problems there are often well hidden.
rows.why: There's usually a reason why people sell. A tired landlord is a fine reason, but a hidden body corporate issue is not.
rows.source: Plaud: 09-07 Consultation: Mercedes - First Home Purchase (2026-09-07)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: units, first home, value, body corporate, land value
rows.hook: The unit type we quietly like: old, small block, no lift.
rows.so_what: Ask why the body corporate fees are what they are before you fall for a view.
rows.insight: Older, smaller unit blocks (around 10–15 one- or two-bedroom units on a decent-sized block, no lift) are a type we like for value. They can be a niche find, but they tend to hold their value.
rows.why: They have low body corporate costs because there are no lifts, and the land underneath gives future appeal to developers.
rows.source: Plaud: 09-07 Consultation: Mercedes - First Home Purchase (2026-09-07)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: rentvesting, investment vs home, living at home, borrowing capacity
rows.hook: Own home or investment first? That's a life question, not a maths one.
rows.so_what: Decide how you want to live for the next five years before you decide what to buy.
rows.insight: Buying a home to live in versus buying an investment first is a lifestyle call. Both are valid. If you can keep living at home, buying an investment first can lift borrowing capacity because rental income counts, but there's nothing like owning your own place.
rows.why: An investment purchase lets rent cover most of the mortgage and opens up growth areas, while owning your home brings security and freedom: no vacating and no inspections.
rows.source: Plaud: 09-07 Consultation: Mercedes - First Home Purchase (2026-09-07)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: mortgage stress, first home nerves, inflation, income growth
rows.hook: Your mortgage feels biggest on day one. It gets easier.
rows.so_what: Plan your buffer for the first two years, because that's when it bites.
rows.insight: A mortgage can feel intimidating at the start, but in our experience it gets cheaper and easier to manage as time goes on. The first couple of years are the hardest.
rows.why: Inflation erodes the real value of the debt, and incomes, especially early in a career, tend to rise.
rows.source: Plaud: 09-07 Consultation: Mercedes - First Home Purchase (2026-09-07)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: refinancing, broker value, loan structure, rates
rows.hook: If all you want is a sharper rate, call your bank.
rows.so_what: Ask how your loans are split and secured, not just what rate they're on.
rows.insight: If all you want is a sharper rate, you can usually just call your bank. Our value is in structure: setting loans up so they're tax-efficient, keep cash flow healthy and help you grow a portfolio.
rows.why: Banks are competitive on price, so rate alone rarely justifies a change. The lasting wins come from how the debt is split and secured.
rows.source: Plaud: 10-09 Consultation: Loan Structuring for Granny Flat Construction, Cash Flow Buffer, and Borrowing Capacity Improvement (2026-10-09); Plaud: 09-18 Consultation: Unit Trust Commercial Property Financing, Guarantor Obligations, and Tax Structure (2026-09-18)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: refinancing, fixed rates, switching costs
rows.hook: We won't move a loan just to move it.
rows.so_what: Before refinancing, ask what the switch adds beyond a slightly lower rate.
rows.insight: We won't move a loan just to move it. If you already have a good rate, especially a good fixed rate, and we can't add a real structural benefit like a needed cash-out, we'd rather leave it alone.
rows.why: Breaking a competitive fixed rate or refinancing for a marginal gain costs more in fees and hassle than it saves.
rows.source: Plaud: 08-05 Client Consultation: Investment Property Pre-Approval and Macau House vs Unit Strategy (2026-08-05); Plaud: 10-09 Consultation: Loan Structuring for Granny Flat Construction, Cash Flow Buffer, and Borrowing Capacity Improvement (2026-10-09); Plaud: 09-18 Consultation: Property Purchase & Loan Strategy (2026-09-18)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: refinancing, construction top-up, discharge costs, switching
rows.hook: Your current bank can often do what you need. Ask them first.
rows.so_what: Before moving, ask whether a top-up or variation with your lender gets the same result.
rows.insight: Where the existing lender can do what's needed, such as a top-up or a construction increase, we try to keep the loan there before looking elsewhere.
rows.why: Staying put avoids discharge and switching costs and makes for an easier journey; we only switch if the rate or structure is meaningfully better elsewhere.
rows.source: Plaud: 08-11 Customer Consultation: Construction Finance for Renovation and Extension (2026-08-11); Plaud: 08-13 Consultation: Property Portfolio Refinancing and Tax-Deductible Loan Strategy (2026-08-13)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: lender choice, borrowing capacity, portfolio growth
rows.hook: Different banks win at different things. Use more than one.
rows.so_what: Ask which lender is strongest for the job you need done now, not overall.
rows.insight: Different lenders win on different things. For a refinance we may prioritise the sharpest rate, then use a different lender for the next purchase where borrowing capacity matters more.
rows.why: Matching each loan to the lender that's strongest for that job beats putting everything with one bank.
rows.source: Plaud: 08-14 Customer Consultation: Loan Refinancing, Debt Recycling, and Investment Structure (2026-08-14)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: interest only, good debt vs bad debt, negative gearing, offset
rows.hook: Pay down your home loan first, not the investment loan.
rows.so_what: Ask your accountant which of your loans your spare cash should be hitting.
rows.insight: Our general view is to keep investment debt on interest-only and focus repayments on your home loan. Investment debt is 'good debt' because the interest is deductible; home loan debt is 'bad debt' because it isn't.
rows.why: Paying down an investment loan reduces your deductions, while paying down the home loan cuts non-deductible interest. The exception is if you plan to move into the investment later.
rows.source: Plaud: 09-18 Consultation: Property Purchase & Loan Strategy (2026-09-18); Plaud: 09-15 Client Consultation: Related-Party Property Purchase, Independent Valuation, and Loan Restructuring Strategy (2026-09-15); Plaud: 08-13 Consultation: Property Portfolio Refinancing and Tax-Deductible Loan Strategy (2026-08-13)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: offset accounts, next home deposit, interest only, upgrading
rows.hook: Planning to upgrade? Build your next deposit inside an offset.
rows.so_what: Ask whether an offset on your investment loan should be where your savings live.
rows.insight: If you own an investment and plan to buy your next home, we like an interest-only investment loan with an offset that you build aggressively. When you buy, the offset money becomes a bigger deposit on the new home.
rows.why: While it sits in the offset you save interest, and once it's withdrawn the investment interest, which is deductible, rises while your non-deductible home loan stays smaller.
rows.source: Plaud: 09-18 Consultation: Property Purchase & Loan Strategy (2026-09-18)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: redraw, debt recycling, tax deductibility, split loans
rows.hook: Money in redraw isn't savings. Treat it that way.
rows.so_what: Before pulling redraw for an investment, ask about a separate split instead.
rows.insight: Money in redraw has effectively paid down your home loan. If you later pull it out for an investment, it muddies the loan purpose. A cleaner approach is to reduce the home loan limit and set up a separate split for investing, which is effectively debt recycling.
rows.why: Keeping the investment borrowing in its own split reduces non-deductible debt and increases deductible debt. It takes careful planning, some costs and accountant input.
rows.source: Plaud: 08-14 Customer Consultation: Loan Refinancing, Debt Recycling, and Investment Structure (2026-08-14); Plaud: 09-07 Consultation: First-Home Purchase Strategy and Borrowing Capacity for Pilot and Event Manager (2026-09-07)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: line of credit, equity release, interest only, offset, investment readiness
rows.hook: Equity sitting ready costs nothing until you use it.
rows.so_what: Ask whether a pre-approved split parked in an offset beats scrambling later.
rows.insight: When we release equity for a future investment, we often set it up as an interest-only facility with the funds parked in an offset. Until you actually use it, your effective repayment is zero.
rows.why: You have the funds ready to deploy, and repayments only start, and become deductible, when the money is used for the investment.
rows.source: Plaud: 08-14 Customer Consultation: Loan Refinancing, Debt Recycling, and Investment Structure (2026-08-14); Plaud: 10-09 Consultation: Celeste - Refinancing and Loan Structuring (2026-10-09)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: equity, cash-out split, cross-collateralisation, stamp duty, deposit
rows.hook: Keep your home and your investment in separate lanes.
rows.so_what: Ask that the deposit comes from a separate split, not by tying both properties together.
rows.insight: With strong equity, we prefer to fund an investment's deposit and costs through a separate cash-out split against your home, without cross-collateralising the properties.
rows.why: Keeping securities separate keeps you flexible, and a separate split used for the investment keeps the interest on that portion deductible.
rows.source: Plaud: 09-15 Client Consultation: Related-Party Property Purchase, Independent Valuation, and Loan Restructuring Strategy (2026-09-15)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: houses vs units, capital growth, rental yield, regional markets
rows.hook: If you can afford it, buy the house.
rows.so_what: Ask what a house in a proven area costs versus the unit you're looking at.
rows.insight: If you can afford it, a house beats a unit as an investment almost every time, on both capital growth and, in many family-oriented regional markets, rental demand.
rows.why: Houses grow faster in value. Units only make sense if borrowing capacity forces it or it's an exceptional deal.
rows.source: Plaud: 08-05 Client Consultation: Investment Property Pre-Approval and Macau House vs Unit Strategy (2026-08-05)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: regional investing, small towns, data, risk
rows.hook: Cheap isn't the same as good value in a small town.
rows.so_what: Ask for the data before you buy somewhere just because it's affordable.
rows.insight: We're cautious about small towns that just look cheap. Unless there's solid data showing strong returns, you're taking a real risk on whether they grow at all.
rows.why: Thin markets lack data to support prices, and the same budget often buys a much better property in a proven market.
rows.source: Plaud: 08-05 Client Consultation: Investment Property Pre-Approval and Macau House vs Unit Strategy (2026-08-05)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: subdivision, dual occupancy, valuations, duplex
rows.hook: Two homes on one title? Check what splitting them is worth.
rows.so_what: Ask a valuer how the two would be valued separately before you decide.
rows.insight: If you own a property with two dwellings on one title, it's worth looking at whether subdividing makes sense.
rows.why: Valued separately, the two properties can come in much higher than they would together.
rows.source: Plaud: 10-09 Consultation: Loan Structuring for Granny Flat Construction, Cash Flow Buffer, and Borrowing Capacity Improvement (2026-10-09)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: related-party purchase, family sales, stamp duty, valuation
rows.hook: Buying from family? Get your own valuation, not just the bank's.
rows.so_what: Ask your accountant and conveyancer what paperwork keeps a family sale clean.
rows.insight: When buying from a family member or another related party at a friendly price, we recommend getting an independent valuation (not just a bank valuation) so the transaction stays clean from a tax and stamp duty point of view.
rows.why: In a non-arm's-length deal, the authorities look at market value, so documenting it independently protects both sides.
rows.source: Plaud: 09-15 Client Consultation: Related-Party Property Purchase, Independent Valuation, and Loan Restructuring Strategy (2026-09-15)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: business cash flow, working capital, line of credit, home equity
rows.hook: The cheapest money for a business is usually secured by a house.
rows.so_what: Ask what a property-secured facility would cost versus the overdraft, and whether you'd want the home involved.
rows.insight: When a growing business needs cash, credit secured by residential property is usually the cheapest form of funding, compared with an unsecured business line of credit or overdraft. It can be lent on to the business through a loan agreement. But if you want the family home kept out of the business, we respect that and look at business-only options.
rows.why: Residential security attracts much lower pricing than business facilities.
rows.source: Plaud: 08-14 Capital Strategy Meeting: Business-Only Funding Alternatives to Scale Inventory Without Personal Collateral (2026-08-14)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: trade finance, working capital, security, pricing, term deposits
rows.hook: Want a better rate on business funding? Offer security.
rows.so_what: Ask how much partial security would move the price before accepting the first quote.
rows.insight: For larger trade and working-capital facilities, security is the biggest lever on pricing. Fees across the major banks tend to be similar, so offering property or cash security (such as term deposits) is what moves the rate.
rows.why: Banks will want some security for a facility of meaningful size, and partial cover, for example about 30–40% of the limit, gives them a lot of comfort.
rows.source: Plaud: 09-21 Consultation: Australian Cosmetics Distributor Financing, Supplier Terms, Inventory Turns, and FX Hedging (2026-09-21)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: property development, private lending, capitalised interest, feasibility
rows.hook: No repayments during the build sounds good. The risk moved, not disappeared.
rows.so_what: Ask what happens to the debt if the units don't sell on time.
rows.insight: Larger townhouse developments are funded on the project's feasibility rather than your income, often with private lending on capitalised interest over 12–24 months. You don't face monthly repayments, but you carry stock risk: if units don't sell, the debt is still due.
rows.why: It's high risk, high reward. Rates around 10–11% plus 1–2% establishment, with interest compounding, mean profitability matters more than repayments.
rows.source: Plaud: 10-09 Consultation: Jay - Property Development Funding (2026-10-09)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: dual occupancy, small development, construction loans, private vs bank
rows.hook: Two or three townhouses? Don't pay private-lender prices.
rows.so_what: Ask whether a mainstream construction loan can fund the project before going private.
rows.insight: For a first, smaller project such as two or three dwellings, we'd rather keep it in mainstream construction lending than pay private-lender pricing, provided the land price is reasonable.
rows.why: If you can get the same result while saving a couple of percent on rate and fees, there's no reason to pay for private money.
rows.source: Plaud: 10-09 Consultation: Jay - Property Development Funding (2026-10-09)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: joint ventures, development partners, trusts, asset protection
rows.hook: Building with a mate? Don't do it in your own names.
rows.so_what: Ask your accountant about a trust or company before you sign anything together.
rows.insight: If you're doing a property project with a partner, we'd recommend a trust or company structure (with accountant input), not your individual names.
rows.why: It limits personal liability, and pooling two strong borrowers can support a much larger project with mainstream lenders.
rows.source: Plaud: 08-14 Customer Consultation: Loan Refinancing, Debt Recycling, and Investment Structure (2026-08-14)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: unit trusts, loans to trusts, negative gearing, accounting
rows.hook: Lending money to your own trust? Write it down properly.
rows.so_what: Ask your accountant whether a formal loan agreement is needed before the funds move.
rows.insight: If you're borrowing personally and putting the money into a unit trust to buy property, check with your accountant whether you need a formal loan agreement between you and the trust.
rows.why: Documenting the loan properly supports claiming the interest on the split you borrowed from.
rows.source: Plaud: 09-18 Consultation: Unit Trust Commercial Property Financing, Guarantor Obligations, and Tax Structure (2026-09-18)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: commercial valuations, lease expiry, capex, lender credit
rows.hook: One wrong assumption can knock a commercial valuation. Find it.
rows.so_what: Ask the valuer for the reasoning behind each assumption, then argue the one that matters.
rows.insight: When a lender questions a commercial valuation, we go back to the valuer for the reasoning behind each assumption (refurbishment allowances, lease expiry dates, capex escalation) and put most of our effort into the one with the biggest impact on value.
rows.why: Assumptions such as treating a tenant's early-termination option as the lease expiry can change value and serviceability, so understanding the reasoning lets us argue the case properly.
rows.source: Plaud: 09-30 Valuation Challenge Negotiation with Lender: Refurbishment Allowances, Lease Term Interpretation, and Capex Escalation (2026-09-30)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: bridging finance, buying before selling, settlement dates, offsets
rows.hook: Bridging finance is usually the expensive way to solve a timing problem.
rows.so_what: Ask whether lining up settlement dates or using equity gets you there instead.
rows.insight: We try to avoid bridging finance. If settlement dates are only days apart, it's better to negotiate the dates to line up, and an offset or line of credit against existing equity can often do the same job.
rows.why: Bridging can cost thousands of dollars, so it only makes sense when there's a big gap between the sale and the purchase, not a few days.
rows.source: Plaud: 10-09 Consultation: Celeste - Refinancing and Loan Structuring (2026-10-09)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: offset accounts, savings, family money, interest
rows.hook: Cash in a savings account is working for the bank, not you.
rows.so_what: Ask what moving your savings into an offset would save you each month.
rows.insight: Cash just sitting in a savings account is often better in an offset against your mortgage.
rows.why: In savings you pay tax on the interest you earn; in an offset you save interest on the loan instead, which isn't taxed, and the money stays accessible.
rows.source: Plaud: 10-09 Call with Quan: First-Time Homebuyer Loan Strategy (2026-10-09); Plaud: 09-07 Consultation: Mercedes - First Home Purchase (2026-09-07)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: construction loans, renovations, progress payments, repayments
rows.hook: Building? You don't pay on the whole loan from day one.
rows.so_what: Ask how repayments step up through each stage of the build.
rows.insight: With a construction loan you don't pay on the full amount from day one. Funds go out as progress payments to the builder, usually interest-only, so repayments rise gradually as the build goes on.
rows.why: That keeps holding costs down during the build, and with existing equity much of the build can be funded without large out-of-pocket amounts.
rows.source: Plaud: 08-14 Customer Consultation: Loan Refinancing, Debt Recycling, and Investment Structure (2026-08-14); Plaud: 08-11 Customer Consultation: Construction Finance for Renovation and Extension (2026-08-11)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: loan applications, documents, self-employed, trusts
rows.hook: We ask for the minimum paperwork first. Always.
rows.so_what: Ask your broker what the lender really needs before sending everything you own.
rows.insight: We go in phases with paperwork: payslips first, then tax returns, and only complex trust or company documents if we really need them.
rows.why: Asking for the minimum needed keeps the process quick and less painful for busy clients.
rows.source: Plaud: 08-11 Customer Consultation: Construction Finance for Renovation and Extension (2026-08-11)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: equity release, quick settlement, existing property, restructuring
rows.hook: The quickest deposit is often sitting in a property you already own.
rows.so_what: Ask how much equity you can release and how fast, before a slower option.
rows.insight: If you have a low loan balance against an existing property, releasing equity from it is often the quickest way to fund a purchase, and the structure can be tidied up later if needed.
rows.why: It can avoid waiting on slower or more complex approvals while reaching the same outcome.
rows.source: Plaud: 09-21 Consultation: Property Financing and Equity Release (2026-09-21)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: why use a broker, lender policy, rate changes
rows.hook: Lending rules change almost daily. That's half our job.
rows.so_what: Ask what's changed in lender policy since you last looked, not just rates.
rows.insight: Lending policy changes almost daily, especially around rate movements, which is a big part of why we do the research and lender legwork for you.
rows.why: Things like how lenders assess borrowing capacity after a rate change can shift within days, and keeping on top of that is a full-time job.
rows.source: Plaud: 10-09 Call with Quan: First-Time Homebuyer Loan Strategy (2026-10-09)
rows.status: From Aadi's recorded calls (Plaud), 21 Oct 2026. Confirm wording on first use.

rows.applies_to: refinance,homeowners,first-home-buyers,lvr
rows.hook: A few thousand dollars can buy you a cheaper rate for life.
rows.so_what: Ask what your loan-to-value is today and how far you are from the next pricing tier.
rows.insight: When a valuation brings you close to 80% of the property's value, we'd rather tip you under the line with a modest lump sum and reprice with your existing lender than discharge and move. Same bank, same offsets, better rate, no exit fees.
rows.why: Crossing the 80% threshold is where pricing steps down, and a small payment often costs less than the discharge and setup fees of a full refinance.
rows.quote: If we stay with the bank, we just get a better rate and nothing else changes.
rows.source: Plaud: Mortgage refinance call (2026-08-18)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: homeowners,refinance,variable-rate
rows.hook: Your rate will move. Your discount shouldn't.
rows.so_what: Ask your broker or bank what discount is written into your contract, not just today's rate.
rows.insight: When we negotiate a variable rate, what we are really negotiating is the discount off the bank's standard rate, and that discount is locked in for the life of the loan. The bank can move rates up or down, but your margin below everyone else stays.
rows.why: Clients often fear a negotiated rate will snap back to the standard rate on the next move; it does not, it moves by the same increment as everyone's.
rows.quote: It's basically a higher discount built in for the life of the loan.
rows.source: Plaud: Mortgage refinance call (2026-08-18)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: refinance,homeowners,investors,working-style
rows.hook: The rate on your proposal is where the haggling starts, not ends.
rows.so_what: Ask your broker whether they re-price before settlement, and how often.
rows.insight: A rate we quote at proposal is a starting point, not a finish line. We keep going back to the lender's pricing desk in the background right up until approval or settlement, and if the market moves or we hear a sharper number is possible, we chase it.
rows.why: Lender pricing shifts week to week and the quoted rate at application is rarely the best one available by the time the loan settles.
rows.quote: We just keep on fighting in the background, back and forth.
rows.source: Plaud: Refinancing, tax planning and development funding (2026-08-18)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: house-and-land,construction,regional
rows.hook: Add up land plus build, then look at what's already standing nearby.
rows.so_what: Pull three comparable established sales before you sign a land contract.
rows.insight: Before committing to a house-and-land package we want you to price it against established homes in the same area. If land plus build lands well above what finished houses are selling for, the new build has to justify that gap on quality, not just on being new.
rows.why: Land prices in growth corridors can rise quickly and a build-plus-land total can quietly overtake comparable established stock.
rows.quote: Have you compared this to what existing houses you're finding?
rows.source: Plaud: Home loan borrowing capacity, house and land (2026-08-07)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: construction,house-and-land,builders
rows.hook: A brand new home is only as new as the builder who built it.
rows.so_what: Ask the builder for addresses of homes they finished five years ago and go and look.
rows.insight: We tell clients who are drawn to building because they are sick of maintenance problems that the builder matters more than the newness. A low-quality builder shows up as the same issues in five to seven years; a quality builder is what you're actually paying for.
rows.why: A new house is only low-maintenance if it was built well, and the price difference between builders is usually smaller than the repair bill later.
rows.quote: With a low quality builder, we might start to see the same issues in the next five to seven years.
rows.source: Plaud: Home loan borrowing capacity, house and land (2026-08-07)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: house-and-land,conveyancing,contracts
rows.hook: Never sign a land contract the developer hands you without a lawyer.
rows.so_what: Get the contract reviewed before you sign, and tell your broker the expected title date.
rows.insight: We will not let a client sign a land contract from a developer without a conveyancer or solicitor reviewing it first, and we refer one if they don't have one. Titling dates, sunset clauses and finance timing all live in that contract.
rows.why: Developer land contracts set the settlement and finance timeline, and an unread clause can leave you needing to settle before your approval is ready.
rows.quote: You should get the contract reviewed before you sign. It's very important.
rows.source: Plaud: Home loan borrowing capacity, house and land (2026-08-07)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: grants,settlement,deposit,construction
rows.hook: Treat the grant as a bonus, never as your deposit.
rows.so_what: Keep enough of your own cash aside to settle without the grant, and chase the grant afterwards.
rows.insight: We plan settlements as if a government grant might not land in time. Grants can be reassessed or declined at the last minute, and if the settlement figures relied on that money the shortfall has to come from your own pocket on the day.
rows.why: Grant approvals sit outside the lender's and broker's control, and a late decline turns a smooth settlement into a scramble for funds.
rows.source: Plaud: Settlement shortfall, grant appeal and construction next steps (2026-08-05)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: pre-approval,employment,parental-leave,casual-work
rows.hook: Don't change jobs or go on leave before your loan is sorted.
rows.so_what: Tell your broker about any upcoming leave or job move before you apply, not after.
rows.insight: If parental leave, a job change or a move from casual to permanent is on the horizon, we'd rather get your approval done on today's payslips and not change anything until we've seen the numbers. It's not impossible afterwards, just slower and more paperwork.
rows.why: Lenders assess what they can see on current payslips; once income changes they ask for employer letters, return-to-work confirmation and more evidence.
rows.quote: It's just a matter of it being more bureaucratic.
rows.source: Plaud: SMSF commercial purchase and construction loan structure (2026-08-07); Plaud: Home loans, pre-approval strategy and refinance top-up (2026-08-06)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: employment,casual-work,nursing,borrowing-capacity
rows.hook: Going permanent isn't always the move. Sometimes casual borrows more.
rows.so_what: Send your broker every payslip from every employer before deciding to change roles.
rows.insight: Casual shift work with penalty rates, especially in nursing, can produce a higher assessable income than a part-time permanent role once you have a few months of payslips. So we don't tell clients to go permanent by default; we look at the payslips first and slice the income properly.
rows.why: Many lenders accept casual income after three to six months with the same employer, and penalty-loaded casual pay often beats the base of a permanent role.
rows.source: Plaud: Home loans, pre-approval strategy and refinance top-up (2026-08-06); Plaud: Home loan borrowing capacity, house and land (2026-08-07)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: upgraders,selling,buying,bridging,timing
rows.hook: Buy first, sell second, and move house once instead of twice.
rows.so_what: Ask what settlement period the seller will accept, then have your broker model buying first with your own savings and no bridging.
rows.insight: When a client's savings can cover the deposit and costs on the next home, we'd rather they buy first on a longer settlement and list the current home the day after, with no bridging loan. The savings go in, the sale proceeds come back out; the end position is the same but you only move once.
rows.why: Selling first forces you into a rental or a rushed purchase, while buying first with your own funds means you move when you want to, not when you have to.
rows.quote: You will only move out when you want to move out, rather than when you have to move out.
rows.source: Plaud: Home loans, pre-approval strategy and refinance top-up (2026-08-06); Plaud: Financial strategy and property planning (2026-09-07)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: upgraders,buyers-agents,selling-agents,advice
rows.hook: Ask who gets paid when you take their advice.
rows.so_what: Decide buy-first or sell-first on your own finances, then brief the agents on your plan.
rows.insight: The buyer's agent will tell you to buy first and the selling agent will tell you to sell first, because that is what gets each of them paid. We ask clients to isolate that advice, run the numbers with us, and then let the agents do their jobs.
rows.why: Both agents can be good at what they do and still give advice shaped by their own timeline and fee.
rows.quote: The buyer's agent would tell you to buy first. The selling agent would tell you to sell first.
rows.source: Plaud: Home loans, pre-approval strategy and refinance top-up (2026-08-06)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: buyers-agents,negotiation,budget
rows.hook: Tell the agent your budget, not your limit.
rows.so_what: Agree your walk-away number with your broker before you brief anyone else.
rows.insight: When a buyer's agent asks whether you'd stretch above budget, we suggest telling them the number you want to stick to and holding the real headroom back. If something genuinely special turns up, that's when you push, not before.
rows.why: Once an agent knows your true ceiling, every property they bring you tends to drift towards it.
rows.quote: Almost tell them that this is what we'd like to stick to.
rows.source: Plaud: Home loans, pre-approval strategy and refinance top-up (2026-08-06)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: upgraders,pre-approval,timeline,working-style
rows.hook: The bank is the quick bit. The timing is the hard bit.
rows.so_what: Map your sale campaign and settlement dates with your broker before you list.
rows.insight: Once you're approved, stepping the pre-approval up or extending it is an email and a contract of sale. The slow parts are finding the property, the sale campaign and lining up settlement dates, so we spend our effort coordinating those rather than worrying about the bank.
rows.why: A strong pre-approval with the same lender can be varied quickly, whereas campaign timing and settlement windows are what actually cause the squeeze.
rows.quote: Finance would be the fastest part of this entire process.
rows.source: Plaud: Home loans, pre-approval strategy and refinance top-up (2026-08-06)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: couples,offset,joint-loans,structure
rows.hook: Two offsets, one loan: shared mortgage, separate savings.
rows.so_what: Ask for multiple offset accounts when the new loan is set up, not after.
rows.insight: On a joint home loan we set up more than one offset account, one for each partner, so each keeps their own savings visible and working against the same debt. For day-to-day privacy, a card in your own name with the same bank does the job without piling up debt.
rows.why: Couples want shared interest savings without merging every dollar, and multiple offsets deliver both.
rows.quote: We create multiple offset accounts. Give one to each of you.
rows.source: Plaud: Home loans, pre-approval strategy and refinance top-up (2026-08-06)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: credit-score,refinance,applications
rows.hook: A home loan application is not the credit-score hit people fear.
rows.so_what: Avoid multiple card or personal loan applications in the months before a home loan; the mortgage itself is fine.
rows.insight: Clients worry that a refinance or restructure application will dent their credit score. In our experience a mortgage enquiry usually holds or lifts the score; it's read as responsible use of credit because you are building an asset, unlike a run of personal loan or card applications.
rows.why: Credit scoring treats secured property lending differently from unsecured credit shopping.
rows.quote: A mortgage inquiry is listed as responsible use of credit. You're actually building an asset.
rows.source: Plaud: Mortgage refinance call (2026-08-18)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: construction,house-and-land,progress-payments
rows.hook: One loan for land and build saves money and headaches.
rows.so_what: If your land is settled and you're about to build, ask whether it can be one application.
rows.insight: When land is already settled and the build is coming, we'd rather do land and construction in one application than add a separate construction split. The bank holds the build funds, your cash contribution reduces the interest-bearing balance from day one, and progress payments just flow.
rows.why: A separate principal-increase application means separate evidence at every stage and your deposit sitting with the builder earning nothing instead of offsetting debt.
rows.quote: It becomes a smoother process. This is just me telling you from experience.
rows.source: Plaud: SMSF commercial purchase and construction loan structure (2026-08-07)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: construction,interest-only,cash-flow
rows.hook: While you're building, pay interest only. Principal can wait for the keys.
rows.so_what: Ask for interest-only through construction and a switch to principal and interest at completion.
rows.insight: During a build we keep the loan interest-only. You're usually paying rent, land interest and then build interest as each builder invoice is paid, and the loan balance rises month by month, so interest-only keeps the cash flow survivable until the house is complete.
rows.why: Lenders can't sensibly set principal on a balance that changes with every progress payment, and the household is carrying rent at the same time.
rows.quote: Interest only helps to sort of cushion that.
rows.source: Plaud: SMSF commercial purchase and construction loan structure (2026-08-07)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: construction,builders,progress-payments,fees
rows.hook: A fee that gets a professional to check your builder's work is cheap.
rows.so_what: Ask how your lender verifies each progress claim before paying the builder.
rows.insight: Some lenders charge a construction fee because they send a valuer to check works at each progress stage before releasing money. We recommend that even over fee-free lenders: it's a second set of eyes making sure the builder is following the contract.
rows.why: A lender that releases progress payments without inspecting is taking the risk on the dwelling and leaving you to police the builder alone.
rows.quote: The builder can't cut corners because the bank is actually making a visit frequently.
rows.source: Plaud: SMSF commercial purchase and construction loan structure (2026-08-07)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: investors,developers,owner-occupied,borrowing-capacity
rows.hook: Shrink the home loan first. It unlocks the next one.
rows.so_what: Before an investment or project, ask how much home debt you can clear and what it does to capacity.
rows.insight: Where a client plans another purchase or project, our mindset is to get the owner-occupied debt as low as we can first. A lower home loan does two things: it improves how the next application services, and it leaves the deductible side to carry the weight. The tax side of that is one for your accountant.
rows.why: Non-deductible home debt is the most expensive debt to carry and the one that most limits the next step.
rows.quote: The more I can reduce your owner occupied, the better, because it will give you more borrowing capacity.
rows.source: Plaud: Refinancing, tax planning and development funding (2026-08-18)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: investors,offset,redraw,loan-hygiene
rows.hook: Park it in the offset. Don't touch the redraw.
rows.so_what: Ask for an offset on every split and use that, not redraw, for everything.
rows.insight: When we set up investment or business-purpose splits we draw the funds into an offset and ask clients never to transact through redraw. The money sits there costing nothing in interest until it's used, and the loan itself stays clean for your accountant.
rows.why: Mixing personal transactions through a redraw blurs what the loan was used for, while an offset keeps the facility untouched and the interest saving identical.
rows.quote: You shouldn't transact through redraw at all. I only want you to transact through offsets.
rows.source: Plaud: Refinancing, tax planning and development funding (2026-08-18)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: loan-term,borrowing-capacity,repayments,investors
rows.hook: Sign for thirty years. Pay it off in twenty-five anyway.
rows.so_what: Take the longest term available and set your own higher repayment or offset target.
rows.insight: Clients often ask to keep a 25-year term to match their old loan. We'd rather write it over 30 and have you pay it like 25. The 30-year term protects your borrowing capacity for the next project; the extra repayments and offset do the actual work of paying it down.
rows.why: Serviceability is assessed on the contracted minimum repayment, so a shorter term on paper costs capacity without saving a cent you couldn't save voluntarily.
rows.quote: What's on paper versus what we do in practice can be two different things.
rows.source: Plaud: Refinancing, tax planning and development funding (2026-08-18)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: market,timing,buyers,investors
rows.hook: When everyone's nervous, that's usually when you buy.
rows.so_what: Get your pre-approval sorted now so you can act on an off-market opportunity.
rows.insight: When headlines are negative and clearance rates are low, we see it as a buyer's window rather than a reason to wait. People are afraid to sell, off-market deals appear, and a client whose budget hasn't moved after meeting buyer's agents is a sign the market is speaking.
rows.why: Property behaves like any market: uncertainty pushes prices down and the rewards go to buyers with finance ready when others hesitate.
rows.quote: People are afraid to sell, and that's why off-market transactions are happening.
rows.source: Plaud: Refinancing, tax planning and development funding (2026-08-18); Plaud: Home loans, pre-approval strategy and refinance top-up (2026-08-06)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: developers,development-finance,small-projects
rows.hook: Small project? Use a home loan. Big one? Let the project borrow.
rows.so_what: Tell your broker the real project size early so the right funding path is planned from the start.
rows.insight: For a one or two dwelling project we start with residential lending because it's cheaper and simpler. Only when the numbers outgrow what your personal income can service do we move to development finance, where the lender assesses the project's feasibility and end values instead, but expects a 20 to 25 percent contribution.
rows.why: Residential policy is the cheapest money for a small project; development funding is for when the project, not the borrower, has to carry the assessment.
rows.quote: They won't go against your personal income. They will do a feasibility study.
rows.source: Plaud: Refinancing, tax planning and development funding (2026-08-18)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: investors,structure,future-purchases
rows.hook: Set up this loan for the house after this one.
rows.so_what: Tell your broker your five-year plan before the loan is structured, not after settlement.
rows.insight: We structure today's loan with the next property in perspective, not just the current one. If this home becomes an investment later, where the debt sits, whose name it's in and how the splits are drawn all matter, and we want those set now. The ownership and tax questions get worked through with your accountant.
rows.why: Restructuring after the fact costs fees and can be impossible once purpose and capacity have changed.
rows.quote: I'm structuring the loan by keeping that next land in perspective as well.
rows.source: Plaud: SMSF commercial purchase and construction loan structure (2026-08-07)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: construction,investors,lender-choice,fees
rows.hook: Saving a fee is pointless if the bank lends you less.
rows.so_what: Ask what each lender's maximum is, not just what each one charges.
rows.insight: When a property will become an investment and we know a later top-up won't be available, we'll pick the lender offering more borrowing capacity even if their fees are higher. A cheaper lender that lends you less today can leave you short for the plan you actually have.
rows.why: Fees are a one-off; a capacity shortfall shapes what the property can do for years.
rows.quote: Better to go with the lender offering more borrowing capacity, even though it's costing us a little more.
rows.source: Plaud: SMSF commercial purchase and construction loan structure (2026-08-07)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: smsf,commercial,business-premises
rows.hook: Don't pour all your super into the deposit.
rows.so_what: Ask what the minimum deposit is for the fund and keep the rest as buffer.
rows.insight: On an SMSF purchase we try to keep the deposit from super as low as the lender allows, around 20 percent plus stamp duty, so the fund keeps a buffer for costs and contributions. The structure itself is simpler than people expect; it comes down to what the fund can service from rent plus contributions. Contribution strategy is one for your accountant.
rows.why: A fund that empties itself into the deposit has no room for settlement costs, vacancies or a rate move.
rows.quote: We'll try to keep the deposit towards the super as low as possible.
rows.source: Plaud: SMSF commercial purchase and construction loan structure (2026-08-07)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: commercial,lender-choice,relationships
rows.hook: Same price from two banks? Pick the one that'll actually deliver.
rows.so_what: Ask whether a term sheet is credit-endorsed or just the banker's opinion.
rows.insight: When two lenders are in line on price, we progress with the one where a relationship exists or where credit has already endorsed the terms. Certainty of execution is worth more than a few basis points on a deal that has to settle.
rows.why: A term sheet that credit has signed off on won't move; an indicative number from a lender you've never settled with can.
rows.quote: Given that we don't have a relationship with you guys, we'd rather progress the transaction forward.
rows.source: Plaud: Term sheet, working capital and security structure (2026-08-13); Plaud: Real estate portfolio financing (2026-08-05)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: commercial,term-sheets,negotiation,working-style
rows.hook: Always have a second bank's offer in writing before you commit.
rows.so_what: Ask your broker who the backup lender is and whether their terms are on paper.
rows.insight: On a sizeable commercial deal we run several lenders in parallel, tell the front-runner they're leading, and still get a formal written term sheet from the second so there is a real backup if security or terms shift late. Surprises happen; a written alternative is the insurance.
rows.why: Lenders have changed security structures at the last minute before, and a verbal backup is no backup.
rows.quote: Surprises do happen, which is why a good backup matters.
rows.source: Plaud: Lender options, valuation and deal structure (2026-08-06); Plaud: Real estate portfolio financing (2026-08-05)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: commercial,covenants,investment-property,credit-policy
rows.hook: The cheapest loan can be the one that chokes you first.
rows.so_what: Ask how far your rental income can fall before the lender's covenant is breached.
rows.insight: On commercial property debt we weigh covenants alongside price. A lender whose interest cover test lets income fall by half before a breach gives you room through a short tenancy or a vacancy; one that trips at a 25 percent fall becomes the path of most resistance the moment something changes.
rows.why: The covenant is the lender's trigger to intervene, so headroom is what keeps a good deal from becoming a forced conversation.
rows.quote: That's why covenants would basically matter in terms of path of least resistance.
rows.source: Plaud: Lender options, valuation and deal structure (2026-08-06)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: commercial,valuation,development-potential
rows.hook: A permit doesn't borrow money. Rent does.
rows.so_what: Ask what the valuer's basis is before paying for any extra valuation scope.
rows.insight: A commercial valuer will assess highest and best use as the asset stands today, and a bank will lend on that, not on permits or a future development scheme. Paying for a separate development valuation only makes sense if you have a use for it beyond the loan, because the lender won't fund the upside.
rows.why: Lenders price risk on current income, so a higher development value is a cost to you with no extra borrowing attached.
rows.quote: The banks are not going to give you more, even if they value it higher.
rows.source: Plaud: Lender options, valuation and deal structure (2026-08-06)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: commercial,security,gsa,renewal,negotiation
rows.hook: Ask the bank for favours when they need you, not before.
rows.so_what: Diarise your facility renewal and bring every ask to that one conversation.
rows.insight: If you want an incumbent lender to release a general security or loosen terms, we raise it at facility renewal when margin and hedging are also on the table, not out of nowhere mid-term. Ask with nothing to trade and the answer is no; ask when they have to fight for the business and it's a negotiation.
rows.why: Lenders concede security positions only when they risk losing the facility, which is at renewal.
rows.quote: At that time, we'll basically have both negotiations in our hands.
rows.source: Plaud: Lender options, valuation and deal structure (2026-08-06)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: commercial,trusts,security,gsa,structure
rows.hook: One lender, one entity, one asset. Keep them in their lanes.
rows.so_what: Ask which entity the lender wants security over, and say no to anything beyond that asset.
rows.insight: When a group has an incumbent bank holding a general security over the master entity, we fund the new acquisition in its own sub-trust or SPV, give the new lender first security over that vehicle only, and get a carve-out deed from the incumbent. Each lender sits on its own asset and nothing is cross-tied.
rows.why: Letting a new lender reach the master entity, or an old lender reach the new asset, cross-collateralises the whole group and makes every future refinance harder.
rows.source: Plaud: Term sheet, working capital and security structure (2026-08-13); Plaud: Real estate portfolio financing (2026-08-05); Plaud: Lender options, valuation and deal structure (2026-08-06)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: trade-finance,invoice-finance,working-capital,overdraft
rows.hook: Work out where your cash is stuck before picking a loan.
rows.so_what: Map the days between paying suppliers and getting paid by customers before you talk to a lender.
rows.insight: Before talking products we work out where the cash gap actually sits. If customers pay you in days but suppliers need paying weeks before stock lands, that's a front-end problem and trade finance fits; if you're waiting on debtors, invoice finance does; if it's lumpy and small, an overdraft may be all you need.
rows.why: Businesses often ask for the facility they've heard of rather than the one that matches their cycle, and the wrong product is expensive or gets declined.
rows.quote: It's pretty much funding the front end of the transaction.
rows.source: Plaud: Trade finance for a cosmetics brand (2026-08-11); Plaud: Skincare business trade finance (2026-08-06)

rows.applies_to: business-lending,security,family-trust,overdraft
rows.hook: Your house should not be the bank's safety net for your business.
rows.so_what: Ask what the facility looks like unsecured first, then what the minimum security would be.
rows.insight: For business facilities we start unsecured or with the smallest security the lender will accept, and if property has to come in, we offer an investment property held in a trust before anyone's family home. Directors with multiple businesses especially should keep their personal mortgage untouched.
rows.why: Once the home secures business debt, every future personal refinance and every business wobble becomes entangled.
rows.quote: They don't want to do their own home, so they'd rather not touch that.
rows.source: Plaud: Overdraft for complex finances (2026-08-06); Plaud: Trade finance for a cosmetics brand (2026-08-11); Plaud: Skincare business trade finance (2026-08-06)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: startups,trading-history,trade-finance,business-lending
rows.hook: Two years of history is the bank's problem. Make your story the answer.
rows.so_what: Prepare your directors' experience and signed customer contracts alongside the financials.
rows.insight: Under two years of trading is the hurdle banks keep tripping on. When a business is young but growing, we lead with the directors' track record in other businesses, the contracts in hand and the growth story, and we're prepared to stack funding from a couple of sources rather than wait for one bank to feel comfortable.
rows.why: Credit teams are conservative on short ABN history, but strong directors and contracted demand are what actually de-risk the deal.
rows.quote: My main concern in this transaction would be the trading length, but they are growing fast.
rows.source: Plaud: Trade finance for a cosmetics brand (2026-08-11); Plaud: Skincare business trade finance (2026-08-06)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: commercial,process,working-style,documents
rows.hook: Give the bank everything at once and watch how fast it moves.
rows.so_what: Ask your broker for the full document checklist before you send anything.
rows.insight: On commercial deals we aim to hand credit everything in one go: financials, trust deeds, leases, rent roll, the agreement, the lot. A complete pack lets the banker workshop it with credit once and come back with endorsed terms, instead of a month of drip-fed questions.
rows.why: Every missing document restarts the credit queue, and a lender who has to chase information prices in the hassle.
rows.quote: Assuming that I can get all the information to you hopefully in one go.
rows.source: Plaud: Real estate portfolio financing (2026-08-05); Plaud: Trade finance for a cosmetics brand (2026-08-11)
