rows.applies_to: upgraders,owner-occupiers,market-timing
rows.hook: Selling at a loss hurts less when you're buying in the same market.
rows.so_what: If you're upgrading, judge the move on the price gap between the two homes, not the loss on one.
rows.insight: Selling for less than you paid stings, but if you're buying in the same market you get that discount back on the way in. What actually costs you is sitting out and waiting for the perfect moment.
rows.why: Upgraders transact in both directions at once, so a soft market largely nets out; being out of the market when it turns is the real risk.
rows.quote: It's probably when you're staying out of the game that it hurts you more.
rows.source: Plaud: Financial strategy and property planning (2026-09-07)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: first-home-buyers,upgraders,market-timing,stamp-duty
rows.hook: Property prices move on the news, not the start date.
rows.so_what: If a concession has been announced, ask how soon you can realistically be ready to buy.
rows.insight: Big policy changes like stamp duty concessions move prices when they're announced, not when they start. If you're planning to transact, we'd rather you move before the headline than after it.
rows.why: Buyers price in extra spending power as soon as they hear about it, so waiting for the rule to take effect usually means paying more.
rows.quote: The market will act on the news.
rows.source: Plaud: Financial strategy and property planning (2026-09-07)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: upgraders,families,school-fees,affordability
rows.hook: That scary future bill is smaller than you think, twice over.
rows.so_what: Model big future expenses against where your income will likely be, not where it is today.
rows.insight: When clients worry about a cost years away, like private school, we point out it gets cheaper on two fronts: inflation erodes it, and your income usually grows into it.
rows.why: People stress-test today's income against tomorrow's bills and talk themselves out of a move that would be comfortable by then.
rows.quote: It does get cheaper with time.
rows.source: Plaud: Financial strategy and property planning (2026-09-07)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: all-borrowers,borrowing-capacity,upgraders
rows.hook: The bank's maximum is not your number.
rows.so_what: Ask for the comfortable figure and the stretch figure, then plan on the first.
rows.insight: When we quote your borrowing capacity we give the comfortable number first. We can usually squeeze more if we push, but you don't want to live at the edge of what a bank will lend.
rows.why: Approval and affordability are different things; the extra hundred thousand rarely buys a better life.
rows.quote: That's being conservative. If we were to push it, I think we can squeeze in another hundred thousand.
rows.source: Plaud: Financial strategy and property planning (2026-09-07)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: upgraders,owner-occupiers,offset,professionals
rows.hook: Upsizing? Keep cash back for the first few years of the bigger loan.
rows.so_what: Ask what the repayments look like and how much buffer you'd have left after settlement.
rows.insight: When you step up to a bigger mortgage, we'd rather use a slightly smaller deposit and keep a healthy offset than tip everything in. The buffer is there to get used to the higher repayments for the first two or three years.
rows.why: The first years of a larger loan are when household budgets wobble; cash in offset costs you nothing and buys breathing room.
rows.source: Plaud: Financial strategy and property planning (2026-09-07)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: upgraders,sellers,market-timing
rows.hook: Not selling for a year? Start talking to agents now anyway.
rows.so_what: Get two appraisals this month and a quick update each quarter.
rows.insight: Even if a sale is a year away, we tell clients to get a couple of agent appraisals now and check in every two or three months. You want to know how your suburb is moving before you have to decide.
rows.why: A live read on value removes the biggest unknown in an upgrade plan: what the current home will fetch.
rows.quote: Keep in touch with them every two or three months to see how the market's flowing.
rows.source: Plaud: Financial strategy and property planning (2026-09-07)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: business-owners,families,planning,idle-cash
rows.hook: You probably can't do everything at once. So which comes first?
rows.so_what: Write down your three big goals and rank them before your next finance conversation.
rows.insight: Before we talk about any product, we try to pull out what the client actually wants, the dream home, the school fees, the money sitting idle, and work backwards from there. Most people can't do everything at once, so the job is to put it in order.
rows.why: Without a priority order, idle cash and competing goals lead to paralysis or random decisions.
rows.source: Plaud: Lazy money and tax optimisation (2026-09-08)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: investors,portfolio,refinance,loan-splits
rows.hook: Selling one property is the best time to clean up all your loans.
rows.so_what: Before settlement, list every loan split and what it was used for, then ask how the structure should look afterwards.
rows.insight: When an investment property sells, we use that moment to tidy the whole structure: clear the splits tied to it, and re-secure any remaining investment debt as its own clearly labelled split so the purpose is obvious. Check the deductibility side with your accountant.
rows.why: Years of top-ups leave loans whose purpose nobody can trace, which costs you at tax time and confuses every future application.
rows.source: Plaud: Refinancing and debt restructuring (2026-09-09)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: all-borrowers,application-process,documents
rows.hook: Your payslip has an expiry date. Banks won't tell you that.
rows.so_what: Keep your last two payslips and current statements handy for the whole application, not just day one.
rows.insight: Payslips and statements have a shelf life with lenders, usually around 60 days. We refresh anything close to expiry before we lodge rather than let a stale document stall the file.
rows.why: A document that times out mid-assessment resets the queue and can push a settlement date.
rows.source: Plaud: Refinancing and debt restructuring (2026-09-09); Plaud: Client acquisition strategy, urgent settlement (2026-09-14)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: couples,self-employed,investors,lender-selection
rows.hook: Why we sometimes put your two properties with two different banks.
rows.so_what: If you're a mixed PAYG and self-employed couple, ask whether one lender or two gives you the better outcome.
rows.insight: For couples where one is PAYG and one is self-employed, we'll often hold properties with two different lenders: the straightforward security in the PAYG partner's name with one bank, the shared one elsewhere. Best of both worlds, and no single bank is exposed to everything.
rows.why: Lenders differ in appetite for self-employed income, and splitting security limits how exposed you are to any one bank's policy change.
rows.quote: We'll basically get the best of both worlds.
rows.source: Plaud: Refinancing (2026-09-10)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: investors,interest-only,offset,refinance
rows.hook: A slightly higher rate can be the smarter loan. Here's when.
rows.so_what: Ask what the rate difference costs in real dollars per year before you give up a structure to save it.
rows.insight: On an investment loan that will sit fully offset anyway, a rate a few basis points higher is worth accepting if it means keeping the structure you want. On a typical loan that gap is a few hundred dollars a year, and on an investment loan it's usually deductible (check with your accountant).
rows.why: Chasing the last tenth of a percent while giving up a usable structure is a bad trade.
rows.quote: It is higher, but it's not higher by a lot.
rows.source: Plaud: Refinancing (2026-09-10)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: co-owners,separation,equity-release,guarantors
rows.hook: Co-owner won't be on the loan? They might not need to be.
rows.so_what: If you share a property with someone, ask whether a security-only guarantee would get you there.
rows.insight: A co-owner can sign as a security guarantor so you can borrow against a jointly owned property without us needing their income at all. Security guarantee and servicing guarantee are different things, and most people only need the first.
rows.why: It unlocks equity in shared property, including after a separation, without dragging the other person's finances into the application.
rows.quote: She doesn't have to be a servicing guarantor. You can just go by yourselves.
rows.source: Plaud: Finance structuring, property separation, super (2026-09-11)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: business-owners,smsf,commercial-property,premises
rows.hook: Your business already pays rent. Why not pay it to your own super?
rows.so_what: Ask your accountant and broker together whether an SMSF should own your next premises.
rows.insight: If you run a business and need premises, our default view is that the building belongs in your super fund where possible: the business pays market rent to the fund, the fund pays the loan, and you build the asset while expensing the rent. Confirm the detail with your accountant.
rows.why: It turns a cost the business already has into an asset the owner keeps.
rows.quote: You expense it through the business. Pay the super. The super pays the loan.
rows.source: Plaud: Finance structuring, property separation, super (2026-09-11); Plaud: SMSF residential property investment ban (2026-09-29)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: business-owners,smsf,commercial-property,yield
rows.hook: Buying a factory in your super? The rent has to beat the interest.
rows.so_what: Before you fall for a property, get a rental appraisal and compare the yield to today's commercial rates.
rows.insight: For a commercial purchase inside super, we want the yield up near the interest rate, around seven percent as a minimum when rates are in the high sevens. Servicing leans on the lease and the rental appraisal, so the property has to earn its keep.
rows.why: Inside super you can't prop up servicing with personal income; the lease and contributions carry the loan.
rows.quote: I'd aim for somewhere around seven at the very minimum.
rows.source: Plaud: Finance structuring, property separation, super (2026-09-11)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: smsf,investors,commercial-property,regulation
rows.hook: Your super fund can't borrow for a house any more. A factory, yes.
rows.so_what: Check with your accountant or adviser what your fund can still buy before you keep saving for a plan that no longer works.
rows.insight: Since 10 August 2026, a self-managed super fund can no longer borrow to buy residential property; it can still buy residential outright with its own cash, and it can still borrow for business premises. If you were building super towards a geared residential purchase, that plan needs a rethink with your accountant.
rows.why: Existing loans set up before the change are grandfathered, so the people affected are those who were saving towards a new one.
rows.quote: Commercial property would be the only way we can put an asset under superannuation now.
rows.source: Plaud: SMSF residential property investment ban (2026-09-29)
rows.status: fact-checked 31 Oct 2026 (Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 1) Act 2026; MFAA, ATO guidance) Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: referral-partners,accountants,business-building, behind-the-scenes
rows.hook: If your referrals only flow when you nag, you don't have a system.
rows.so_what: Map the three moments in a partner's workflow where a finance question naturally comes up, and script the handoff.
rows.insight: Referral partnerships that run on one person's energy fade the moment that person gets busy. It has to be built into the partner's own process, with clear trigger points, so it stops being extra work and becomes part of looking after their client.
rows.why: It's a behavioural problem, not a conceptual one: partners agree in principle and still don't refer unless the moment is obvious.
rows.quote: This is a behavioral challenge. Like it's not a conceptual challenge.
rows.source: Plaud: Redesigning a referral engine (2026-09-11)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: referral-partners,accountants,advisers, behind-the-scenes
rows.hook: Mentioning finance isn't selling. It's noticing.
rows.so_what: If your accountant has never asked about your loans, ask them why not.
rows.insight: When accountants hesitate to raise finance with a client, it's because it feels salesy. Our view is the opposite: flagging that a car loan is due or a business is about to buy equipment is a value-add, and it makes the adviser look better, not pushier.
rows.why: Clients expect their adviser to notice these things; silence is the worse service.
rows.quote: They should be having these conversations because it's value add to the client. It makes them look better.
rows.source: Plaud: Redesigning a referral engine (2026-09-11)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: asset-finance,referrals,client-service, behind-the-scenes
rows.hook: When we hand you to someone else, we ask one question first.
rows.so_what: Ask any adviser who refers you on how they vetted the person they're sending you to.
rows.insight: When we refer something we don't do in-house, like asset finance, the only question we ask about the partner is what service our client will get. The referral fee is irrelevant if the experience is worse than ours.
rows.why: Our name is on the introduction, so the client judges us on how the partner treats them.
rows.quote: What kind of service is my client getting? That's the only one.
rows.source: Plaud: Redesigning a referral engine (2026-09-11)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: business-building,positioning,referral-partners, behind-the-scenes
rows.hook: Never say 'free'. Say 'it's on us'. The difference is huge.
rows.so_what: Next time you give something away, name the cost you're covering instead of calling it free.
rows.insight: We don't describe a bundled service as 'free'. Free sounds like no work was done and makes people wonder what they're losing. We say 'your bill is on us', because there's still a bill, someone is just covering it.
rows.why: With a premium partner the perceived value of advice has to survive the offer; 'free' quietly destroys it.
rows.source: Plaud: Cross-selling finance/accounting, 'on us' pitch (2026-09-16)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: settlement,buyers,sellers,conveyancing
rows.hook: A settlement delay hurts someone you've never met. Check first.
rows.so_what: Before requesting an extension, ask your agent what the other party has planned around the date.
rows.insight: If settlement has to slide, we check what it does to the people on the other side before we ask. A seller may have the removalists booked; a buyer may have given notice. The deal still gets done, but we don't do them dirty.
rows.why: A delay you barely notice can wreck someone else's week, and goodwill matters if you need their cooperation later.
rows.quote: We wouldn't want to do them dirty. Just in case they've made plans.
rows.source: Plaud: Client acquisition strategy, urgent settlement (2026-09-14)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: settlement,buyers,contracts
rows.hook: Need more time to settle? Ask once, and ask for all of it.
rows.so_what: Find out what penalty-free extension your contract allows before you need it.
rows.insight: When a settlement needs more time, we take the whole penalty-free window the contract allows rather than a day or two. Asking twice is worse than asking once for enough.
rows.why: Banks and lawyers rarely hit a tight revised date; a second extension request damages trust and can trigger penalties.
rows.quote: Let's just max it out and I'll keep you posted.
rows.source: Plaud: Client acquisition strategy, urgent settlement (2026-09-14); Plaud: Client banking, PEXA settlement (2026-09-22)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: first-home-buyers,car-finance,budgeting
rows.hook: Just bought a house? Statistically, a car is next. Plan it.
rows.so_what: Decide now how you'd fund a car in the next year, before you commit to a repayment.
rows.insight: Most people who buy a home buy a car within six months, and they replace cars every two and a half years, not the five everyone assumes. So we talk about the car when we set up the home loan, not after it has blown the budget.
rows.why: A car loan taken on just after settlement is the most common way a carefully planned mortgage becomes tight.
rows.quote: Everyone says five, but people change it sooner.
rows.source: Plaud: Client acquisition strategy, urgent settlement (2026-09-14)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: first-home-buyers,pre-approval,lender-selection,urgency
rows.hook: The cheapest lender is often the slowest. Which matters more right now?
rows.so_what: Tell your broker how close you are to making an offer; it changes which lender is right.
rows.insight: Smaller lenders often have the sharpest rates and the slowest assessment. If you're about to make an offer, we'll switch to a major bank for speed and wear a few hundred dollars a year; if there's no rush, we wait for the better rate.
rows.why: A great rate is worthless if the approval arrives after someone else has bought the house.
rows.quote: All the smaller banks have really good rates. They're a bit painful to work with on the assessment stage.
rows.source: Plaud: Client banking, PEXA settlement (2026-09-22)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: first-home-buyers,buyers,conveyancing,contracts
rows.hook: Conveyancer or solicitor? Only one can tell you what the contract means.
rows.so_what: Before you sign anything, ask whether the person reviewing it is allowed to give you legal advice.
rows.insight: We prefer clients use a solicitor rather than a conveyancer. Both can do the conveyancing, but only a solicitor can advise you on the contract itself, which is exactly what you need during negotiations, repairs and special conditions.
rows.why: The expensive mistakes happen in the contract, not in the title transfer.
rows.quote: Technically conveyancers can't advise you on contract law.
rows.source: Plaud: Client banking, PEXA settlement (2026-09-22)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: first-home-buyers,buyers,building-and-pest,due-diligence
rows.hook: Old house, better inspector. New house, save your money.
rows.so_what: Tell your inspector the property's age and condition before you choose the level of report.
rows.insight: We don't have one building and pest inspector, we match the inspector to the property. Older or rougher house, the more thorough and more expensive report; newer, mid-range property, the cheaper one does the job.
rows.why: The thoroughness you pay for should scale with the chance of finding something.
rows.quote: If it's super old, then we'll go for the more expensive one.
rows.source: Plaud: Client banking, PEXA settlement (2026-09-22)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: investors,portfolio,settlement,refinance,selling
rows.hook: Selling and refinancing on the same day? That's where settlements break.
rows.so_what: If you're selling one property and refinancing others together, ask who is paying out each loan and how.
rows.insight: When a sale and a refinance of other properties settle on the same day, the way the outgoing lender handles the discharge can break everything. We now confirm up front how each lender will treat each loan account, and build in time.
rows.why: It's rarely the numbers that fail; it's two banks and a settlement platform disagreeing about who pays out what.
rows.source: Plaud: Client banking, PEXA settlement (2026-09-22); Plaud: Loan payout and discharge discrepancies (2026-09-24)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: first-home-buyers,new-migrants,nurses,essential-workers,employment
rows.hook: New job, no payslips yet? You might not have to wait.
rows.so_what: Send your broker the contract the day you sign it, not the first payslip two months later.
rows.insight: If you're a nurse or in a similarly steady profession and new to the country, a signed employment contract is often enough for us to get finance moving. You don't always need months of payslips first.
rows.why: Lenders treat some professions as low-risk, so the start date matters more than the history.
rows.quote: The moment you get a job, even a contract, we can use that to get the finance approval.
rows.source: Plaud: Mortgage and vehicle financing (2026-09-28)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: car-finance,novated-lease,payg,families
rows.hook: Leasing a petrol car through work? Check the maths first.
rows.so_what: Before signing a novated lease, ask for a side-by-side with a standard car loan on the same car.
rows.insight: A novated lease is usually only worth it for an electric vehicle. On a petrol car the lease often ends up expensive, and a plain car loan can be the better deal. We run your payslip through both before recommending either.
rows.why: The tax treatment that makes a lease attractive is skewed towards EVs; without it you're paying for packaging, so it's worth checking the numbers with your accountant.
rows.quote: More often than not, lease is only beneficial if you are doing an electric vehicle.
rows.source: Plaud: Mortgage and vehicle financing (2026-09-28)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: first-home-buyers,families,borrowing-capacity
rows.hook: Kids won't stop your home loan. They will shrink it a bit.
rows.so_what: Ask what living expenses the lender assumes for your household size, not just what you actually spend.
rows.insight: Having kids never stops an approval, but each dependant pushes up the living expenses the bank assumes, which eats into borrowing capacity. We'd rather you know that going in than find out at the numbers stage.
rows.why: Assessed household expenses, not just your spending, drive the capacity calculation.
rows.quote: You're allowed to have kids, of course, but at the same time it does push your household expenses up.
rows.source: Plaud: Mortgage and vehicle financing (2026-09-28)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: investors,equity-release,loan-splits,pricing
rows.hook: The size of your deposit changes the rate you're offered.
rows.so_what: Ask what LVR band your loan falls in and what it would take to drop into the next one.
rows.insight: When you have equity in your home, we'll often pull the deposit and stamp duty out as a separate split and keep the new investment loan at 70 percent LVR, because that's where lender pricing improves. Three clean splits, each with a purpose, priced as one package.
rows.why: Lenders price by LVR band, so sizing the deposit to land on the right band buys a better rate on the whole deal.
rows.quote: Seventy percent of that, so that we get better pricing.
rows.source: Plaud: Refinancing + investment loan structuring (2026-09-21)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: all-borrowers,refinance,rate-negotiation, behind-the-scenes
rows.hook: Banks give better rates when they know who else you're talking to.
rows.so_what: Before accepting any rate, ask what competitor pricing was put in front of the lender.
rows.insight: We never ask a lender to sharpen a rate without a competitor's pricing in hand. We run the request with a second bank first, then ask the preferred lender to match or beat it, and escalate if the first answer is weak.
rows.why: Discretionary pricing teams respond to a named competitor far more than to a polite request.
rows.quote: Add them as a competitor. You'll get a much better result.
rows.source: Plaud: Refinancing + investment loan structuring (2026-09-21); Plaud: Transaction overview, CBA credit process (2026-09-23)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: all-borrowers,identity-checks,credit-file,application-process
rows.hook: A middle name on your credit file can stall your home loan.
rows.so_what: Pull your credit report before you apply and make sure every name on it matches your ID.
rows.insight: Lender identity checks are far stricter than they used to be. A middle name sitting on your credit file that isn't on your ID, or a professional membership in a previous surname, will stall an application until it's documented.
rows.why: Automated verification can't reconcile mismatches the way a banker with a paper file once did.
rows.source: Plaud: Application meeting: servicing, compliance, contract (2026-09-17)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: first home buyers, property search, way of working
rows.hook: If you'd give up a Saturday to see it, send it to me first.
rows.so_what: Shortlist the homes you would inspect in person and send them to your broker before the open, not after the offer.
rows.insight: Once you know your number, we set up one group chat and ask you to send us only the properties you would actually drive out to inspect. If it is worth your Saturday, it is worth a conversation with us about price, the agent, the offer and the contract.
rows.why: Talking through real candidates early builds the judgement you need to recognise the right one, and it keeps the broker in the loop before an offer is made, not after.
rows.quote: If a property is something that you take the time to go inspect, it's definitely worth us talking about.
rows.source: Plaud: First home loan assessment (2026-10-29)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: first home buyers, self-employed, side income, borrowing capacity
rows.hook: Your weekend trade job can lift your home loan, if it's on paper.
rows.so_what: If you have a side business, ask your accountant how the next return will read to a bank before you lodge it.
rows.insight: A side ABN on top of a wage is not a complication, it is extra capacity. We use both the PAYG income and the business income in the assessment, but only what is declared as net profit actually counts, so talk to your accountant about how you report in the year or two before you buy.
rows.why: Lenders assess the taxable figure from your returns, not the turnover, so a heavily minimised side business adds little even if it turns over a lot.
rows.quote: Given that you have self-employed and PAYG income, we'll make full utilisation of both.
rows.source: Plaud: First home loan assessment (2026-10-29)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: nurses, not-for-profit workers, NDIS, income verification
rows.hook: Salary packaging isn't a tax trick to the bank. It's income.
rows.so_what: Ask your broker which parts of your payslip are being used and what history the lender needs for the rest.
rows.insight: If you work for a charity or hospital and salary-package part of your pay, that packaged amount is real income to us and we present it that way to the lender. Allowances and overtime are different: we only use them once there is a few months of consistent history, otherwise we build the application on base pay.
rows.why: Lenders accept mandated not-for-profit packaging as income because it is structural, but treat variable allowances as unreliable until a pattern is proven.
rows.quote: We have not used allowances income for servicing. We have just used base.
rows.source: Plaud: Land loan / refinance, second recording (2026-10-01)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: buying with family, joint ownership, borrowing capacity, investors
rows.hook: Buying with your brother? Some banks only count half that loan against you.
rows.so_what: Before co-buying, ask how the joint loan will be assessed when one of you wants to buy again.
rows.insight: When you buy with a sibling or friend and later want to borrow on your own, some lenders will only count your share of that joint loan and rent against you. We model it both ways before advising anyone to co-buy, because it decides whether the second purchase is possible.
rows.why: Common debt reducer policies exist at some lenders and not others, so the same two people can be approved or declined depending on where the application lands.
rows.quote: A common debt reducer is basically when you have a debt with someone else... their servicing level is still assessed.
rows.source: Plaud: Pre-approvals, pricing, borrowing capacity (2026-10-12)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: nurses, police, essential workers, owner-occupiers, risk
rows.hook: The safest borrower in Australia is a nurse buying a house to live in.
rows.so_what: If you are an essential worker, ask what lender policies and discounts exist specifically for your profession.
rows.insight: In our experience the lowest-risk borrower in the country is an essential-services worker buying an established home in a metro area to live in. Stable job, stable asset, and nobody hands back the roof over their own family's head.
rows.why: Owner-occupied established metro property has the deepest resale market and the strongest emotional commitment to keep paying, which is why lenders fight for that profile.
rows.quote: That's their home. Anyone, even if they give it back to you, that's their home. They wouldn't want to.
rows.source: Plaud: High-LVR lending fund evaluation (2026-10-08)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: first home buyers, deposit, low deposit lending
rows.hook: Most people can afford the repayments. They can't afford the deposit.
rows.so_what: Ask what deposit you actually need under current schemes before assuming you have to keep saving.
rows.insight: For most working households the thing locking them out of a home is the deposit, not the repayments. That is why we spend our time on deposit pathways, guarantees and low-deposit schemes rather than telling people to wait until they have 20 percent.
rows.why: A couple who can comfortably service a loan at today's rates can still be years away from a 20 percent deposit, and prices rarely wait for them.
rows.quote: We are funding the deposit. That's the whole value premise.
rows.source: Plaud: High-LVR lending fund evaluation (2026-10-08); Plaud: First home loan assessment (2026-10-29)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: fixed vs variable, rate stress, refinancing
rows.hook: Fixing your rate right now means paying more from day one, on purpose.
rows.so_what: Decide what you are buying, certainty or a lower repayment, before you lock anything in.
rows.insight: When fixed rates sit above variable, fixing means accepting a rate rise today in exchange for knowing the repayment for two years. We will fix for a client who needs that certainty to sleep, but we never dress it up as a saving.
rows.why: Fixed rates price in the bank's expectation of where rates go, so the premium is the cost of certainty, and nobody, including us, can predict the Reserve Bank.
rows.quote: The decision is whether we lock it today or not.
rows.source: Plaud: Commercial property financing, capital raise (2026-10-09)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: cash flow stress, car loans, repayments, rate rises
rows.hook: Twenty grand barely dents a mortgage. It can nearly kill a car loan.
rows.so_what: If repayments are tight, ask which debt a lump sum would actually change month to month.
rows.insight: When repayments bite, a spare twenty or thirty thousand does almost nothing against a large mortgage, but it can cut a car loan repayment by hundreds a month. We point stressed clients at the small loan first because that is where the monthly relief is.
rows.why: Repayment relief is proportional to the loan size, so the same dollars shrink a small loan's repayment dramatically and a big loan's by a rounding error.
rows.quote: What's twenty thousand going to do to the mortgage? But for the car loan, yes, it will make a difference.
rows.source: Plaud: Commercial property financing, capital raise (2026-10-09)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: offset, buffers, rate stress, budgeting
rows.hook: Don't ask how much buffer you have. Ask how many months it buys.
rows.so_what: Divide your buffer by the monthly shortfall and write down the date you will review the plan.
rows.insight: If a repayment is too much to carry from income alone, we set a fixed amount the household pays and let the offset or equity cover the gap, then we count how many months that lasts. A buffer expressed as five years of runway is a plan; a buffer expressed as a lump sum is just anxiety.
rows.why: Knowing the exact number of months the gap can be covered turns an open-ended worry into a dated decision point to review, refix, or sell.
rows.quote: I don't want you to lose your sleep over your mortgage, either.
rows.source: Plaud: Commercial property financing, capital raise (2026-10-09); Plaud: Loan covenants, surplus cash (2026-10-01)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: borrowing capacity, pre-approval, lender selection
rows.hook: Your borrowing power isn't one number. It depends who you ask.
rows.so_what: Ask your broker how many lenders your capacity was tested with before you set your price range.
rows.insight: There is no single borrowing capacity. The same payslips run through different lenders' calculators give different answers, so we run several before we tell anyone a number, and we can usually do that within a day of getting documents.
rows.why: Lenders treat overtime, business income, dependants and living expenses differently, so capacity varies materially from one bank to the next.
rows.quote: I'll put it into different banks' calculators and then get back to you with the best outcome.
rows.source: Plaud: First home loan assessment (2026-10-29)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: refinancing, valuations, pricing, timing
rows.hook: Banks go through hungry phases. That's when we push.
rows.so_what: Ask whether now is a good month to refinance based on lender appetite, not just the headline rate.
rows.insight: Lender appetite moves in cycles, and when banks are hungry for business we push harder on valuation and pricing because they have room to say yes. Part of our job is knowing which lenders are hungry this month.
rows.why: A bank chasing volume will stretch on valuation or discount where the same bank six months later would not.
rows.quote: Banks are hungry at the moment, so they're pushing guys to get business, which we'll use to our benefit.
rows.source: Plaud: Nabin refinancing status, valuation (2026-10-08)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: property investors, portfolio review, cash flow, refinancing
rows.hook: If your rentals only just pay for themselves, they're not paying you.
rows.so_what: Write down what your portfolio leaves you each month after every repayment; if it is zero, book a review.
rows.insight: A portfolio where rent almost covers the repayments and you live off your wage is not working for you, it is just surviving. When we review a portfolio we start with what is left over each month, and if the answer is nothing, the structure needs to change before anything else.
rows.why: Zero monthly surplus means any vacancy, repair or tax bill comes straight out of personal savings, which is how investors end up selling at the wrong time.
rows.quote: The rental income is almost covering the repayments. But that's where the tough part comes.
rows.source: Plaud: Liberty loan review, refinancing (2026-10-14)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: property owners, rate stress, selling, holding strategy
rows.hook: A good property can still be the wrong one to keep.
rows.so_what: Separate the two questions: has it done well, and can you comfortably hold it for two more years.
rows.insight: A property that has grown well can still be the wrong one to keep. The question is never whether it was a good buy, it is whether holding it is sustainable for day-to-day living; if it is, we plan to hold and let it grow, and if it is not, selling early and moving to something smaller is a perfectly good decision.
rows.why: Growth on paper does not pay the monthly shortfall, and forced sales later cost more than planned ones now.
rows.quote: How sustainable will it be for your day-to-day living while keeping the property?
rows.source: Plaud: Commercial property financing, capital raise (2026-10-09)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: valuations, refinancing, equity release, selling
rows.hook: The bank's valuation is not what your house would sell for.
rows.so_what: Ask your broker for both numbers, the valuation the bank used and the realistic sale range.
rows.insight: A bank valuation and a sale price are two different numbers for two different jobs. We will push a valuation as hard as we can to get a refinance over the line, but we will also tell you plainly what the market would actually pay if you sold.
rows.why: Valuers working for a refinance can lean on renovations and comparables in a way buyers at auction will not.
rows.quote: Pretty aggressive, but that's what we needed to get the refinance done.
rows.source: Plaud: Nabin refinancing status, valuation (2026-10-08)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: developers, land purchase, construction, self-employed
rows.hook: Buy the dirt first. Borrow for the build when the permits exist.
rows.so_what: If you are planning to build, ask for a land-only loan now and a construction pathway later rather than one application.
rows.insight: If you want to build but do not yet have plans and permits, we fund the land on its own first and leave the construction loan for when the contracts exist. The awkward middle period is hard to service, so the land loan has to stand on today's income and be structured to roll into construction later.
rows.why: Construction pre-approval needs fixed-price contracts and permits, and a land-only loan at a mainstream lender is far cheaper than specialist vacant-land products.
rows.quote: It's not a construction. It's land only at the moment.
rows.source: Plaud: Land loan / refinance (2026-10-01); Plaud: Land loan / refinance, second recording (2026-10-01)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: business owners, vehicle finance, asset finance, debt structure
rows.hook: Your work ute probably shouldn't live inside your home loan.
rows.so_what: Before signing dealer finance, ask your broker and accountant how the vehicle debt should be structured.
rows.insight: If a vehicle is genuinely for the business, we would rather finance it as business debt than roll it into the home loan. The structure can change what the business can claim, so we settle it with your accountant before the dealer's finance desk settles it for you.
rows.why: Mixing business assets into non-deductible home debt loses structure and makes it harder to unwind later, and dealer finance is set up for the dealer's convenience, not yours.
rows.quote: We can structure it in a way that it becomes deductible debt.
rows.source: Plaud: Adviser cross-sell, open banking, asset finance (2026-10-12)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: commercial property, fund structures, LVR, ICR
rows.hook: On commercial deals, the valuation doesn't set your loan. The cash flow does.
rows.so_what: Ask for the lender's interest-cover model and challenge the assumptions driving the weakest year.
rows.insight: On a commercial deal the bank's loan amount is set by interest cover, not by the valuation, so arguing about LVR is really arguing about the year-two cash-flow model. We fight the inputs: refurbishment cost per square metre, incentive assumptions and the exact dates lease clauses bite.
rows.why: A few dollars per square metre of assumed refurbishment or a lease break date moved by months can swing interest cover below the bank's hurdle and cost five percent of LVR.
rows.quote: What's your ICR calculation at the moment for year two?
rows.source: Plaud: Facility coverage, holdbacks, LVR (2026-10-05); Plaud: Valuation assumptions, cash-flow risk (2026-10-01); Plaud: Commercial property financing, capital raise (2026-10-09)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: commercial property, leases, valuations, due diligence
rows.hook: We moved a valuation by reading one clause in a lease.
rows.so_what: Before a commercial valuation, hand the valuer the exact termination mechanics of every lease, with dates.
rows.insight: Valuers model the earliest date a tenant could leave, so we read every termination clause ourselves and go back with the lawyers when the valuer has the date wrong. Moving one break date by a few months improved the valuation on a deal where nothing physical changed.
rows.why: Probability-weighted vacancy drives commercial cash-flow valuations, and the clause wording, not the headline lease expiry, sets that probability.
rows.quote: I did try to argue... they were quite firm on that. So I got some level of improvement.
rows.source: Plaud: Valuation assumptions, cash-flow risk (2026-10-01)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: commercial property, fund structures, covenants, review events
rows.hook: Give the bank a trigger, not your cash.
rows.so_what: Ask whether a review event tied to a specific tenant outcome can replace a permanent cash hold or covenant.
rows.insight: When a commercial deal has a weak year ahead, we would rather offer the bank a designated cash buffer and a review event than accept a hard cash hold or a lower LVR. A review event only bites if the trigger happens; a covenant or a held balance bites every day.
rows.why: Banks need comfort for the stressed year, and surplus raised capital earmarked for the asset gives them that without freezing the client's operating cash.
rows.quote: Is that something that can act as a mitigant? We know that in year three, cash flow will bounce back.
rows.source: Plaud: Loan covenants, surplus cash (2026-10-01); Plaud: Investment fees, ICR, lease renewal cash release (2026-10-29); Plaud: Facility coverage, holdbacks, LVR (2026-10-05)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: commercial lending, redraw, line fees, surplus capital
rows.hook: Parking cash in a commercial loan doesn't switch off the whole bill.
rows.so_what: Ask your banker what portion of the interest a redraw actually offsets before deciding where surplus capital sits.
rows.insight: Parking surplus capital in a commercial facility's redraw saves the base-rate interest but not the line fee, which keeps running on the full limit. If the money is not coming back out, we would rather reduce the limit; if it might, redraw is the price of flexibility.
rows.why: Commercial pricing has two parts, and only the floating component is offset by redraw, so idle capital in a large facility still carries a cost.
rows.source: Plaud: Loan covenants, surplus cash (2026-10-01)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: commercial lending, fund managers, lender relationships, disclosure, behind-the-scenes
rows.hook: Tell the bank the ugly bits first. Surprises cost more than problems.
rows.so_what: Before a commercial submission, list every cash flow leaving the asset and make sure the lender has seen all of it.
rows.insight: Every fee stream, management charge and side arrangement goes to the lender on day one, even the ones that hurt the numbers. A material item surfacing after credit has priced the deal resets the whole conversation, and the goodwill you have built evaporates with it.
rows.why: Lenders can structure around a known weakness, but a late surprise reads as a trust problem and triggers a full re-assessment at the worst possible time.
rows.source: Plaud: Investment fees, ICR, lease renewal cash release (2026-10-29)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: debt consolidation, credit cards, car loans, refinancing, rate stress
rows.hook: One loan you can see beats five small ones you can't.
rows.so_what: List every debt and its repayment, then ask what consolidating all of them into the mortgage would save each month.
rows.insight: When someone has a string of small loans eating their cash flow, the clean fix is a dollar-for-dollar consolidation into the home loan: no extra cash out, every small account closed, one repayment left. Debt secured against a home is almost always the cheapest money you will ever have.
rows.why: Lenders will stretch for a consolidation that clearly reduces monthly outgoings and leaves one liability, but they will not if it is bundled with cash-out or if the old accounts stay open.
rows.quote: So dollar to dollar consolidation. We cannot have anything more, anything less.
rows.source: Plaud: Loan consolidation (2026-10-16); Plaud: Adviser cross-sell, open banking, asset finance (2026-10-12)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: credit file, missed repayments, SMSF lending, refinancing
rows.hook: The bank's failed direct debit shouldn't wreck your credit score. Fight it.
rows.so_what: Pull your credit report before applying, and if a lender's error is on it, lodge a written complaint with evidence.
rows.insight: We run a soft credit check at the start of every application because clients rarely know what is sitting on their file. When a missed repayment is the bank's own failed direct debit, we draft a formal complaint for the client to send with the evidence attached, because a formal complaint gets actioned in days where a phone call gets lost.
rows.why: Two wrongly reported missed payments can drop a score below the thresholds specialist and SMSF lenders require and cost the client their best rate.
rows.quote: It's purely their error. So we'll go on the offensive now.
rows.source: Plaud: Credit file impairments SMSF/refinance (2026-10-13)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: complex applications, credit assessment, way of working, behind-the-scenes
rows.hook: Banks approve stories, not spreadsheets.
rows.so_what: If your situation is unusual, ask your broker what the written case to the lender will say before it is submitted.
rows.insight: Hard deals get approved on the narrative, not the numbers alone. Before we lodge anything borderline we speak to the lender's credit team, get a reference, and write the submission as a story: what went wrong, why it is not a pattern, and exactly how this loan fixes it.
rows.why: Assessors have discretion, and a pre-agreed exception with a clear rationale in the notes survives the handover between the business development manager and credit.
rows.quote: If you mention all of that, I do think it will stick.
rows.source: Plaud: Loan consolidation (2026-10-16); Plaud: Credit file impairments SMSF/refinance (2026-10-13)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: refinancing, settlement, loan amounts
rows.hook: Your refinance will be a bit bigger than your loan. That's deliberate.
rows.so_what: If your new loan amount is slightly above your old balance, ask where the difference goes; the answer should be your offset.
rows.insight: A refinance is always set up for a touch more than the exact payout figure because the old bank charges interest daily right up to settlement. The small surplus lands in your account afterwards; it is not a mistake and not a cost.
rows.why: Payout figures move every day, and a loan that comes up short at settlement delays the whole switch.
rows.quote: Banks charge interest on a daily basis. That's why it's good to have that buffer.
rows.source: Plaud: Pre-approvals, pricing, borrowing capacity (2026-10-12)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: loan documents, interest only, settlement, way of working
rows.hook: Approved isn't the same as written down. Read the loan documents.
rows.so_what: Before signing, check that the repayment type, term and offset match exactly what you were told was approved.
rows.insight: We read the loan documents on the lender portal the moment the deal goes unconditional, before they reach the client, because the structure we fought for, like an interest-only period, has a habit of going missing between approval and contract.
rows.why: Documents are produced by a different team from the one that approved the structure, and fixing an error after signing is far slower than before.
rows.quote: Do check on that. It should have interest only.
rows.source: Plaud: Pre-approvals, pricing, borrowing capacity (2026-10-12)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: new businesses, construction loans, specialist lenders, refinancing
rows.hook: The lender you've never heard of is a stepping stone, not home.
rows.so_what: If you are with a specialist lender, ask what date you will qualify for a mainstream refinance and put it in the calendar.
rows.insight: A specialist or non-bank lender is a stepping stone, not a destination. New businesses under twelve months of ABN and brand-new construction loans often have to start there, so we take the specialist loan to get the job done and diarise the refinance to a mainstream lender the moment the file qualifies.
rows.why: Specialist pricing can sit two percent or more above mainstream, and the qualifying event, ABN age or six months post-completion, is predictable enough to plan around.
rows.quote: To go to majors, that would be something we'd need more ABN length.
rows.source: Plaud: Vehicle finance new business (2026-10-02); Plaud: Credit file impairments SMSF/refinance (2026-10-13); Plaud: Adviser cross-sell, open banking, asset finance (2026-10-12); Plaud: Land loan / refinance (2026-10-01)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: lender selection, way of working, self-employed, unusual security
rows.hook: The cheapest rate from a bank that says no is worthless.
rows.so_what: Ask your broker which policy rules shaped your lender shortlist, not just which rate won.
rows.insight: We check policy fit before we look at rate. Who lends on vacant land, who accepts one year of self-employed figures, who will take this income type: those questions get answered with research tools first, and only the lenders left standing get compared on price.
rows.why: The cheapest rate from a lender whose policy declines the file is worth nothing, and a declined application leaves a mark that follows the client.
rows.quote: Those are the kind of things, and I ask questions all the time.
rows.source: Plaud: Land loan / refinance (2026-10-01); Plaud: Pre-approvals, pricing, borrowing capacity (2026-10-12)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: rate reviews, open banking, client care, refinancing
rows.hook: Your broker shouldn't have to ask you for bank statements twice a year.
rows.so_what: Ask whether your broker uses open banking so rate reviews happen without you chasing paperwork.
rows.insight: With twelve months of open-banking consent we can see a client's current rate and fees without asking them for a single statement, which turns the six-monthly rate review from a favour we ask into a service we just deliver.
rows.why: Clients stop responding to statement requests, so a review that depends on them sending documents quietly dies; consented data removes that friction.
rows.quote: We don't really need to ask them for that information before delivering value.
rows.source: Plaud: Adviser cross-sell, open banking, asset finance (2026-10-12)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: personal insurance, first home buyers, client care, compliance
rows.hook: The loan is approved. Now, who pays it if you can't?
rows.so_what: After approval, ask how much life, disability and income cover you actually have, not whether you have some.
rows.insight: We raise personal protection as a structured step after formal approval, not a line buried in the proposal, and we would rather refer to a proper adviser than push a tick-box policy that does not do the job. If a client declines, they sign a separate document saying so.
rows.why: A new mortgage is the moment a household's exposure is highest, and a product that gives little real cover is not value, it is paperwork.
rows.quote: It is some level of protection, but it's not a great level of protection.
rows.source: Plaud: Broker referral partnership, insurance, super (2026-10-13); Plaud: Adviser cross-sell, open banking, asset finance (2026-10-12)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use.

rows.applies_to: referral partners, conveyancers, advisers, way of working, behind-the-scenes
rows.hook: A good referral isn't a phone number. It's a briefing.
rows.so_what: When your broker refers you on, ask what they have already shared so you are not starting from zero.
rows.insight: When we introduce a client to a conveyancer, planner or adviser, that person walks in already briefed with what our compliance allows us to share. A referral that is just a name and a number tells the client we did not really know them.
rows.why: Referred professionals convert and serve far better when they arrive informed, and the client feels the introduction as an extension of the service rather than a hand-off.
rows.quote: It doesn't really feel like, oh, it's a tick and flick referral.
rows.source: Plaud: Broker referral partnership, insurance, super (2026-10-13)
rows.status: Mined 31 Oct 2026 from Plaud calls (Aug–Oct). Aadi to confirm wording before first use. Confidence: medium.

rows.applies_to: client care, referrals, way of working, rate reviews, behind-the-scenes
rows.hook: Your broker's job starts again the day your loan settles.
rows.so_what: Ask your broker what happens after settlement and when your first scheduled review is.

rows.applies_to: investors,cash buyers,first investment

rows.hook: Fortnightly isn't magic. It's one extra month of repayments a year.

rows.applies_to: investors, equity, offset, deposits, liquidity
